title: Real occluder geometry (icosphere + disc) and correct TLAS placement
purpose: Replace placeholder meshes with proper geometry and place occluders to intersect the particle cloud so ray-query shadows become visibly testable.

steps.detail: Implement CPU-side icosphere generation (subdivisions 2–3). Produce position-only vertex buffer and index buffer with SHADER_DEVICE_ADDRESS_BIT. Radius paramizable (default 3.0).
Implement CPU-side disc/annulus mesh in the XZ plane with N segments (e.g., 128). Parameters: innerRadius (default 1.0), outerRadius (default 6.0).
Rebuild BLAS for both meshes using the new vertex/index buffers and update stored handles.

Create TLAS instances: (1) Sphere at world origin with uniform scale=radius, (2) Disc centered at origin tilted 20–35 degrees around X or Z. Ensure instance transform (3x4, row-major) is populated correctly. Mask=0xFF.

Expose a scene-level light direction (default normalize(-0.5,-0.8,-0.6)) and ensure the occluders sit between light and particles. Add runtime UI/toggles to tweak sphere radius, disc tilt, and light direction for quick validation.
Log occluder instance transforms and bounds once after build. Optionally draw debug wireframe of occluder bounds (toggle) to confirm placement.

acceptance: TLAS updated with two instances (sphere + disc) and non-null device address
Particles visibly darken when occluders intersect them with RT enabled
Debug toggle shows occluder bounds aligned with shadows
notes: VkAccelerationStructureInstanceKHR.transform is a row-major 3x4. Ensure consistent world-space conventions for instance placement and light direction.
